properties.statement:
A VERIFIES EDGE CARRYING AN EXPLICIT `pinned` LIST SILENCES `unverified_enforced_rule` EXACTLY AS AN UNQUALIFIED ONE DOES — the evidence scope is stored and never read by the detector. REPORTED by the dev_storyflow api-boss fleet (`05af57c1`, 2026-08-09, governance trial-case report, finding ①) as `coverage: partial` failing to soften the detector. INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED HERE THE SAME DAY, on a different graph, a different rule and by a different author, within roughly an hour of the rule being created — which is why it is recorded as measured rather than relayed.

THE REPRODUCTION, one variable: rule:per-design-state-is-never-a-process-global was set enforced=true and given ver:no-per-design-process-globals, a real detector with a run negative control. `set_evidence_scope` was then called on the VERIFIES edge pinning three parameters — struct_field_scoping, runtime_behaviour, and whether_a_global_is_semantically_per_design. That third pinned parameter IS THE RULE'S OWN STATED TEST: the rule says in so many words that 'the test is not is-it-a-static but would-this-need-a-different-value-for-a-second-design'. So the edge now declares, in a structured field, that the check does not exercise the rule's central question. `detect_gaps(scope=that rule, depth=1)` afterwards: `unverified_enforced_rule` DOES NOT FIRE, and nothing in the output mentions the pinned list. Before and after are identical.

THE DIRECTION IS THE POINT, and the fleet stated it best: supplying MORE information made the graph LESS accurate, because the extra information is stored and not read. An author who calls set_evidence_scope honestly and an author who never calls it are indistinguishable to the detector — so the tool that exists to record a check's limits cannot make those limits count anywhere.

AND IT IS THIS PROJECT'S OWN WRITTEN GUIDANCE ARRIVING AS A MECHANISM RATHER THAN AS ADVICE. The check-health and governance-proposal skills both say, verbatim: 'Never attach a check to close a finding. Attach it because it detects the violation, and if it does not, say so and leave the finding open.' Both authors DID say so, in the structured field provided for it, and the finding closed anyway. The guidance is currently enforceable only by conscience — which is the same class of defect as an enforced rule with no detector, one level up.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: the two cases differ in severity and that difference matters. The fleet's check never exercised the only path its rule existed to protect (an uncontested CAS standing in for a contended one), so their rule read as detected while its central case was untested. This check DOES cover its clause as literally worded — a new process-global fails the build, proven by planting one in a third crate — and what it pins is the rule's broader semantic test, which no source scan could decide. So the defect being reported is not 'these checks are bad'; it is that THE DETECTOR CANNOT TELL THE TWO APART, and neither can a reader of loop_status.

FIX SHAPES, the fleet's, cheapest first and recorded as theirs rather than adopted: (1) have `unverified_enforced_rule` treat a pinned/partial scope as not-yet-verified, or fire a softer sibling naming the pinned string, since the author already wrote the reason and the gap can quote it; (2) at minimum surface pinned/swept in loop_status's verification digest so a partial check is visibly partial without opening the node; (3) the general form, which is their ratified rule: presence of a check is not adequacy of a check, and a detector that reduces 'is it verified' to 'does a VERIFIES edge exist' can only ever detect the edge disappearing.
